action: As Kai Iwi Lakes advises, be wary of unexpected WhatsApp messages, emails or texts about bookings; do not click links or share payment details, and confirm bookings with the park directly.
date_note: The NZ Herald article, published 23 November, gives no earlier day for the breach or the messages.
exec: A booking provider's reported breach has reached several Northland campgrounds, with customers receiving fake payment requests.
geo_basis: operator region (Kaipara District, Northland) as stated by the article
plain: A booking system used by Northland campgrounds, Seekom, has reportedly been breached. Some campers got WhatsApp messages asking for payment. Kai Iwi Lakes says the messages are not from the council.
summary: The NZ Herald reports that Seekom, a third-party booking system used by Northland campgrounds, has reported a cyber breach, with customers' personal and booking details reported as accessed. Kai Iwi Lakes Campground says it is working with Seekom on the extent and that WhatsApp payment messages did not come from the council. Top 10 Holiday Parks' chief executive said the provider appeared to have been compromised. The article carries no Seekom statement.
title: Northland campgrounds warn customers after reported Seekom booking-system breach

validation.note: Single publisher (NZ Herald / Northern Advocate); Seekom's own statement not in the article.

review.note: Compared title, date, status, summary, action and sectors against the NZ Herald article: Seekom reported breach, Kai Iwi Lakes statement, Top 10 CEO remark and no Seekom statement all match; single_source is right.
